table.text: Key Comparability Caveats — read before using this model

table: VMware, Inc. acquisition closed Nov 22, 2023 (day 1 of FY2024), for $86,290M total consideration (~$54.2B in Broadcom stock, remainder cash). Goodwill $43.7B->$97.9B, intangibles $3.9B->$40.6B, total assets $72.9B->$165.6B, revenue $35.8B->$51.6B. FY2023 and prior are pre-VMware; treat FY2023->FY2024 as a structural break, not organic growth.

Per FY2025 10-K Note 3: 'we included upfront license revenue of $7,800 million within products revenue... we reclassified $4,601 million and $1,058 million of upfront license revenue from subscriptions and services revenue to products revenue for fiscal years 2024 and 2023, respectively.' This model uses each fiscal year's OWN as-filed Products/Subscriptions split (i.e., FY2024 and FY2023 columns are NOT reclassified/recast) — a pure historical series. Do not compare Products vs. Subscriptions growth rates across the FY2023/FY2024/FY2025 boundary without adjusting for this.

Effective July 15, 2024 (within FY2024). FY2016-FY2023 EPS/share-count columns are each year's own pre-split as-filed figures; FY2024 onward are post-split. WASO basic jumps from 415M (FY2023) to 4,624M (FY2024) — roughly 11.1x, reflecting both the 10:1 split and real new share issuance for the VMware deal. Do not compute raw EPS/share-count YoY growth across this boundary.

Broadcom redomiciled from Singapore (Broadcom Limited, CIK 0001649338) to Delaware (Broadcom Inc., CIK 0001730168) on April 4, 2018, accounted for as a common-control transaction (historical financials carried over on the same basis, no restatement). Treated as continuous in this model. Noncontrolling interest (exchangeable LP units) existed FY2016-FY2018 and was eliminated at the redomiciliation.

FY2016-FY2018: 4 segments (Wired Infrastructure, Wireless Communications, Enterprise Storage, Industrial & Other). FY2019 only: 3 segments (Semiconductor Solutions, Infrastructure Software, IP Licensing) following the Nov 2018 CA Technologies acquisition. FY2020-present: 2 segments (Semiconductor Solutions, Infrastructure Software). The SEG sheet presents each structure as a separate block (not stitched together) per the source-hierarchy rule against mixing segment definitions.
6. FY2020-FY2022 segment data sourced from MD&A, not a formal Note

Broadcom's FY2020, FY2021 and FY2022 10-Ks do not include a numeric segment table in the Segment Information note (narrative only in some years); the segment revenue/operating income figures for those years are sourced from each year's MD&A 'Results of Operations' table instead (still Tier-2 SEC-filing sourced, just a different section of the same document).

Broadcom sold the VMware End-User Computing (EUC) business to KKR on July 1, 2024 for $3.5B cash. FY2024's own as-filed income statement includes a 'Loss from discontinued operations, net of income taxes' line of $(273)M; FY2023 and earlier show no such line since EUC was only acquired as part of VMware at the start of FY2024 (no retroactive restatement was required or made).

Income Statement and Segment quarterly columns show the single 13-week quarter ended 2026-08-02. Balance Sheet quarterly column is the point-in-time balance as of 2026-08-02. Cash Flow Statement quarterly column is the cumulative 9-month year-to-date figure as filed (Broadcom's 10-Q does not present single-quarter cash flows) — this is a different grain than the IS/BS quarterly column and is explicitly noted on the CF sheet.

rows.label: Products revenue
rows.note: Products/Subscriptions split first disclosed in FY2019 10-K; not presented separately for FY2016-FY2018 in their own filings. SEPARATELY: starting with the FY2026 Q1 10-Q, Broadcom reclassified 'upfront license revenue' from Subscriptions/services into Products (applied retrospectively to that filing's own FY2025 Q1 comparative column only). The 1Q/2Q/3Q FY2025 quarterly columns in this model are each shown on that quarter's OWN as-originally-filed (pre-reclassification) basis, consistent with the own-quarter/no-restatement rule used throughout this workbook — they are therefore NOT directly comparable, line-for-line, to the FY2025 annual column (which uses the FY2025 10-K's post-reclassification presentation) or to the 1Q/2Q FY2026 columns (also post-reclassification). Total revenue is unaffected in all cases — only the Products/Subscriptions split shifts.

sheets.name: Sources
table: All figures on IS/BS/CF/SEG are Tier-2 (hand-extracted directly from each fiscal year's own SEC 10-K or 10-Q, sourced from the prepared/document.md filing text above). No Tier-1 financial_input.json existed for this company; tables.json (Tier-2 bundle collector output, 994 tables) was reviewed but not used directly for IS/BS/CF because its period-normalization regex did not match full-date column headers (e.g. 'November 2, 2025'), so it produced no usable Income Statement / Balance Sheet / Cash Flow / Segment sheets — see model.draft-bundle.json.bak in this directory for the discarded draft.

Every annual column uses that fiscal year's OWN as-filed figures from its own 10-K, not a later filing's restated/recast comparative column. This preserves a pure historical series but means some comparability breaks are real disclosure changes, not modeling errors — see Cover sheet for the full list (VMware, revenue reclassification, stock split, segment redefinition, discontinued operations).

The original draft model.json (Phase 3 auto-assembly) grouped tables into 7 heuristic topic sheets (Other Notes, Tax & Shares, Products & Geography, Debt & Liquidity, Capital Returns, Assets & Intangibles, Operating KPIs) from unverified bundle data. These were dropped in this rebuild rather than carried forward unverified; the core financial statements (IS/BS/CF/SEG) together with Derived Metrics (DM) are the verified, source-traced deliverable.
